record.title: quantum fundamental groupoid
record.name: QuantumFundamentalGroupoid
record.content:
\subsubsection{Fundamental Groupoid Functors in Quantum Theories} The natural setting for the definition of a \emph{quantum fundamental groupoid} $F_{\Q}$ is in one of the functor categories-- that of \PMlinkname{fundamental groupoid functors}{FundamentalGroupoidFunctor}, $F_{\grp}$, and their \PMlinkname{natural transformations}{NaturalTransformation} defined in the context of quantum categories of quantum spaces ${\Q}$ represented by Hilbert space bundles or `rigged' Hilbert (or Frech\'et) spaces ${\H}_B$.
\begin{definition} The \emph{quantum fundamental groupoid} is defined as $F_{\Q}: \H_B \to {\Q}_G$, where ${\Q}_G$ is the category of \emph{quantum groupoids} and their \emph{homomorphisms}. \end{definition}
\textbf{Note:} Other related \emph{functor categories} are those specified with the general definition of the \emph{fundamental groupoid functor}, $F_{\grp}: \textbf{Top} \to \grp_2$, where \textbf{Top} is the category of topological spaces and $\grp_2$ is the \PMlinkname{groupoid category}{GroupoidCategory}.
\textbf{A specific example} can be given for \emph{spin foams of spin networks}, with spin foams defined as a functor between \emph{spin network} categories. Thus, as spin networks or graphs are specialized one-dimensional CW complexes whose cells are linked quantum spin states their quantum fundamental groupoid is defined as a representation of CW compexes on `rigged' Hilbert spaces, also called Frech\'et nuclear spaces.
